MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD AND THE 
PRESIDENT AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER OF THE MONTREAL YMCA 


The Montreal YMCA ranks among the most important community-based organizations 
in Montreal. In its ten community centres located throughout the area, the YMCA was able to 
provide services to over 65,000 participants during the year thanks to the dedication of its 280 
full-time and 800 part-time employees and approximately 1,000 program and policy 
volunteers. 


Community-based organizations in the Montreal area are called upon to deal with ever 
increasing problems. There are mounting pressures on individuals and families because of the 
high rate of unemployment. This situation is further accelerated by the fact that all levels of 
government are facing a financial crisis and are reducing their spending on social programs. 


In the year ended May 31, 1995, the Montreal YMCA continued to make progress. 
Revenues increased by 4% to reach $21.1 million. After interest charges and the net operating 
costs of the Drummond Tower and Norris buildings, the Association generated a surplus of 
$17,406 compared to a deficit of $74,999 in the previous year. 


The improvement in the surplus from operations was particularly encouraging. In 
fiscal 95 it was $423,879 compared to $63,401 in fiscal 94. Thanks to the efforts of the 
branch directors, the staff and volunteers, the Montreal YMCA is moving towards the levels of 
efficiency which are required in order to assure the Association’s financial viability in the years 
to come. 


The emphasis in fiscal 95 was to improve the infrastructure of the Montreal YMCA. 
The major element of this program was the launch of a study to computerize the operations of 
the Association. We mandated consultants to select appropriate accounting and operations 
software and to conduct a complete review of our practices and procedures. This study was 
completed by year-end. The Centre-ville branch was selected as the test site and we are 
pleased to report that the new system is now installed and is operating successfully. We 
anticipate that all branches will be on the new system by May 1996. 


This is a major initiative for the Montreal YMCA representing an investment of almost 
$1 million. Most staff members are undergoing intensive training and we are beginning to see 
the benefits of having an up to date management information system. This investment will 
permit us to have access to more accurate and timely information thereby enabling us to react 
more quickly to changes in our environment. 


We also began a strategic planning exercise in fiscal 95, the purpose of which is to 
assure that the Montreal YMCA will continue to be relevant in terms of meeting the needs of 
the community in the closing years of this century and the beginning of the next. An integral 
part of the strategic planning process was a market research study which was conducted in the 
summer of 1995 in order to position the Montreal YMCA in each of the four major areas of its 
activity, namely, health, fitness and recreation; child development; continuing education; and 
community development. In-depth interviews were conducted with over 2,000 individuals 
throughout greater Montreal. As a result of the valuable information obtained, the Montreal 
YMCA is better informed and, as such, will be able to focus its activities more effectively to 
maximize the benefits of its efforts within the community. 


With the market research now completed, we must set the objectives for the Association and 
develop the plans required to meet these objectives. This process is underway and will be 
completed by May 1996. 


Another major initiative worthy of note in fiscal 94 1s Priority S.A.M. (Service to Annual 
Members). This isa program launched by YMCA Canada and its purpose is to set standards of 
performance and measure results in terms of service to annual members. This initiative was 
undertaken in response to a general decline in the YMCA’s share of the health, fitness and 
recreation market across Canada. The objective of the program is to improve membership 
retention rates and to reverse the decline in our share of the market. The program entails 
extensive training for staff, upgrading equipment and physical facilities, and improving 
customer service practices. The membership retention rate in the Montreal YMCA is about 
50%. We are confident we will make a significant improvement in this area through our 
participation in Priority S.A.M. Recently, the Board of Directors agreed to make a major 
financial commitment to upgrade and add to our inventory of exercise equipment. 


The Montreal YMCA is proud of its long tradition of helping Montrealers to help 
themselves to improve their quality of life. In fiscal 95, the YMCA subsidized needy 
Montrealers to the extent of over $600,000 to allow them to participate in a number of 
activities several of which are described in the branch highlights. 


The Montreal YMCA continues to face a number of challenges, financial and otherwise. 
But, much progress has been realized in recent years and we have good reason to be optimistic 
about the future. During its long history, the Montreal YMCA has often demonstrated its 
ability to adapt to a changing environment. Throughout, however, its four fundamental values 
of Honesty, Respect, Caring and Responsibility have remained the constant beacon which has 
guided the organization for 144 years. It is our belief in and application of these values which 
will guide us into the next century. 


In closing, we wish to thank our volunteers, our funders, and our members for their 
invaluable support. Without their interest and participation, the accomplishments of the 
Montreal YMCA would simply be impossible. We extend our admiration and our sincere 
appreciation to the employees of the Association. The Montreal YMCA is blessed with a 
competent, enthusiastic and dedicated group of individuals who perform well beyond the call 
of duty and often under difficult conditions. In them, lies the strength of the organization and 
the principal reason why the Montreal YMCA really does make a difference. 


Marcel Côté ns 


Bernard W. Matte 
Chairman of the Board President & Chief Executive Officer 


BRANCH HIGHLIGHTS 


Centre-ville YMCA 


The Centre-ville branch launched two Canada Youth Service programs reaching young 
adults aged 16-25 and one youth recreational and tutorial program for youth aged 13- 
18% 


The branch hosted an International Conference on Children’s Rights bringing together 
delegates from the YMCAs of Nicaragua, Honduras, Ecuador, El Salvador and Montreal. 
Sixteen education and youth workers from outside Canada participated in the event. 


The Residence and Cafeteria both had an excellent year. A systematic remodelling 
program was initiatied in the Residence. 


Du Parc YMCA 


The new Du Parc YMCA was opened on October 7, 1994. The project was completed 
on time and within budget. 


The branch is off to a great start. Membership is ahead of forecast and we balanced the 
budget in fiscal 95. In a recent survey, 90% of respondents stated they were satisfied 
with the programs and 85% said they would renew their membership. 


One of the most successful programs is the youth drop-in centre where upwards of 100 
young people gather every day to participate in activities designed and conducted by 
very capable and caring staff members. 


Guy-Favreau YMCA 


This Was another very active year at the Guy-Favreau YMCA. Ninety people graduated 
from the training sessions to become qualified program volunteers. 


The branch launched its first edition of Quelque Chose, a periodical containing 
information on activities at the centre. Articles are printed in French, English and 
Chinese. 


Subsidies were offered to 171 individuals to permit them to participate in programs. 
Also, the branch’s facilities were made available at no charge to 15 groups in the 
community. These groups include daycare administrators, physically and mentally 
challenged individuals, seniors, and young people at risk. 


The campaign Peluches de Pâques Was once again a great success. We were able to 
give almost 400 stuffed animals to five centres for abused children. 


The annual fundraising campaign exceeded the objective. 


Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA 


One of the highlights this year was our participation in the highly successful march Of 
Bread and Roses. This project involved hundreds of women who marched from 
Montreal to Quebec City to sensitize the population to problems related to poverty. A 
number of people at the branch were involved in this initiative and the Association is 
grateful to them. 


Thanks to the efforts of the fundraising committee, the branch’s campaign results 
exceeded those of last year. Also, through the campaign, the branch increased its 
visibility among the business community. 


In November 1994, two staff members had occasion to visit the branch’s international 
partner, the YMCA of Nicaragua. They renewed the terms of the partnership and 
experienced first hand the positive impact their Nicaraguan colleagues are having in 
that country. In March 1995, a delegation of two from the YMCA of Nicaragua visited 
the branch. 


The day camp, continuing education, membership programs and the arena all 
experienced progress during the year. 


Kamp Kanawana 


In March 1995, Ms. Joanna Hoad was named Kamp Director. Joanna is the first female 
director in the over 100 year history of the Kamp. Under her leadership, the Kamp had 
a very successful 1995 summer season. Camper registration and the return rate 
continued to be among the highest in the country. 


Bruce Netherwood, who served as Kamp Director from 1989 to 1994, moved to Cape 
Cod where he is the Director of Camping Services of the South Shore YMCA in Qunicy, 
Massachusetts. We thank Bruce for his valuable contribution and wish him well with 
his new responsibilities. 


Notre- Dame- de- Grâce YMCA 


Thanks to a committed group of volunteers and a dedicated staff, the NDG YMCA had a 
good year in spite of the challenges presented as a result of operating in an older 
facility. 


Membership remains constant and the branch was very active with community 
development initiatives, a variety of programs for youth and a number of activities 
related to its international partnership. 


Plans were drafted to remodel many areas within the building and subsequent to year- 
end, several projects were in progress to give the branch a major face-lift. 


Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA 


It was a year of many first at the Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA. The biannual newsletter 
À La Fine Pointe / To the Pointe, was launched and distributed to 20,000 households. 
Two members of the staff went to Honduras to develop their international partnership 
with the Honduras YMCA. A new Cooperative Jeunesse Service was established and 
introduced some new partnership models to the municipal housing authority in Little 
Burgundy. 


In light of the changed demographics in the community, the future role of the branch is 
under study. The YMCA is committed to the South West region of the City, but it wants 
to minimize duplication of services with other agencies and to focus on those activities 
which are relevant to the needs of the residents. 


Saint-Laurent YMCA 


After years of effort, the Saint-Laurent YMCA reached an agreement with the City of 
Saint-Laurent to expand the parking lot next to the YMCA facility thus resolving, in 
large meaasure, a major problem for the branch. 


The branch continued to be very active with a number of community projects. There 
are now 150 people in the P.A.LR. program (individual monitoring system for seniors 
living alone). French language courses for immigrants increased in popularity as did 
the community kitchen program. Thanks to a generous grant, 100 children were able 
to participate in their day camp program. 


Westmount YMCA 


Annual membership increased to an all-time high and 1,000 preschoolers participated 
in programs offered by the branch. The Kamp Kinema program was, once again, a 
great success. 


The Westmount YMCA organized special computer olympics and wheelchair basketball 
for National Access Awareness Week. The twice weekly free senior tea and swim 
program run by senior volunteers was very popular. 


West- Island YMCA 


The Family Centre had 4,600 members at year-end. Over 3,000 people participated in 
à la carte adult, youth, and pre-school programs. The centre’s financial development 
efforts this past year were extremely successful by raising $27,500 for their annual 
campaign and $13,000 for their Y-A-THON. 


The Community Centre provided support services to 1,812 young people. These 
services included the Impact program for young offenders, the Diversion Clubs for 
youth in difficulty and the Intersections program for high school dropouts. Sessions 
were offered to over 500 young people on various topics such as shoplifting prevention 
and conflict resolution. Over 250 people with intellectual disabilities took part in social 
and recreational programs, while support was given to an additional 62 disabled 
persons to include them in regular community activities.

Message from the Chairman of the Board, Mr. Charles H. Hantho and the President of the Montreal 
YMCA Foundation, Mr. Richard L. Cooper 


The Montreal YMCA Foundation has just completed its eleventh year of activities. Despite a difficult 
economic climate, revenues for the past year total $434,301, representing a 21.3% increase and expenditures 
increased by 0.52% to reach $135,057. 


While these results are satisfactory, it is important to underline that the major increase in our revenues is 
attributable to our annual campaign among people who are part of the YMCA family, namely the directors 
of the Foundation and of the Montréal YMCA, volunteers, staff members, members and friends of the 
YMCA. We achieved this financial growth thanks to the efforts of the members of the Executive Committee 
who worked within the framework of the adopted plan of action. Their work resulted in additional 
contributions made to the Montreal YMCA, which proved to be essential in these times of uncertainty and of 
social fragmentation. 


In reaching beyond its walls, the YMCA responds to needs which arise in its community. It reaches out to 
the disadvantaged, refugees, youth in conflict and a large number of other people by offering programs which 
are adapted to the current reality. 


Our commitment to the YMCA is particularly important at this time, since it is preparing to launch a capital 
fundraising campaign with a view to redeveloping the Downtown YMCA. 


The Downtown YMCA represents the driving force of the Montreal YMCA and is essential to its financial 
viability. Through its presence in downtown Montreal, the YMCA is able to respond to the vital needs of a 
large part of the Montreal population. 


In closing, we would like to take this opportunity to thank the members of the Board of Directors, and in 
particular those whose term on the Board is ending. We also wish to underline the excellent work 
accomplished by the Foundation team.

Investments, Endowment and Planned Giving 


Presided over by Mr. Maurice A. Massé, the Endowment and Planned Giving Committee pursued its excellent 
work to preserve the heritage of the YMCA. Under the supervision of the Investments sub-committee headed 
by Mr.William Ridley, the investments of the Endowment Fund yielded a book value of $1,765,309. The 
interest and dividends generated by these investments totalled $160,799, of which $90,000 was transferred to

YMCA activities according to the provisions of the designated and non-designated funds. 


The highlight of this division was undoubtedly the annual banquet of the Heritage Club, held on April 25, 
1995, during which Mr. Massé received a well-deserved recognition for his deeply committed and dedicated 
service to the YMCA mission. The tremendous success of this event was due to the efforts of those who 
organized it: William Ridley and Robert Murray. Other members of the Club also contributed to the success 


of the evening. 


Annual Campaign 


Thanks to the sustained efforts of its Chairman, Mr. Robert Vineberg, the Annual Campaign produced 
unprecedented positive results. In fact, a total of $188,120 was raised. Monies received during this campaign 
are committed primarily to subsidies which allow people of all ages to participate in various programs of the 
Montreal YMCA. A portion of this money is also allocated to international-development programs and to 
youth programs. The success of this fundraising campaign was due to the philanthropic spirit of hundreds of 
volunteers and staff members, as well as the generosity of all our donors. 


Y-A-Thon 


This year's Y-A-Thon took place from November 21 to November 27, 1995. A team composed of dynamic 
employees and volunteers organized this event through which the centres of the Montreal YMCA succeeded 
in raising a total of $76,835 allocated to the purchase of equipment. We wish to thank Les Breuvages Nora 
inc. for participating as a major sponsor of this event. 


Benefit Evening 


The Foundation held its annual benefit evening on Friday, February 24, 1995, at Théâtre Saint-Denis. On the 
occasion of this year's benefit we presented a performance of André-Philippe Gagnon's show. We raised 
$69,479 to finance YMCA programs and activities intended for youth both here and abroad. A special thanks 
to our sponsors: Imasco Limited, Télé-Direct (Publications) Inc., St. Lawrence Cement, Hydro-Québec 
and Pratt & Whitney Canada Inc. 


Golf Tournament 


Chaired by Mr. Serge Jacques, the organizing committee of the golf tournament held the tenth edition of the 
annual golf tournament of the Montreal YMCA Foundation. This event, which attracted 160 golfers to the 
Pinegrove Golf Club in Saint-Luc, helped us raise close to $47,626 which was transferred to youth programs 
offered by the Montreal YMCA. To some degree, this was Mr. Jacques’ swan song since, after many years 
of loyal service, he has decided to resign from the Special Events Committee. His presence will be sorely 
missed by each and everyone of us. 


Finally, we wish to thank our patrons of honor for their generosity: The Royal Bank of Canada, Bell 
Canada, St. Lawrence Cement, the Fédération des caisses populaires Desjardins de Montréal et de 
l'Ouest-du-Québec, HCCI Management Services Inc., Lafleur Brown, Langlois Robert, Merck Frosst 
Canada Inc., Montrusco & Associates Inc., ScotiaMcLeod Inc., Téléglobe Canada inc. and Wood 
Gundy Inc. 


We also wish to thank our 26 sponsors and various enterprises which graciously donated the door prizes. 
In addition, we wish to thank all the employees, volunteers and friends of the Montreal YMCA who once 


again, through their collective efforts, helped guarantee the heritage of the Montreal Association for future 
generations.
